theme: The foot washing; “I AM the way”; the Spirit promised
readingInstruction: Read John 13:1-14:31. The Upper Room begins: Jesus washes his disciples’ feet, gives a new commandment, predicts betrayal and denial, and then comforts them with promises of the Father’s house, the Way, and the Holy Spirit. Take your time. These are among the most tender chapters in the Bible.
settingTheScene: It is the night before Jesus’ death. He is in an upper room in Jerusalem with the Twelve. John spends five chapters (13 to 17) on this one evening, and he omits the Lord’s Supper itself. The tone shifts: no more public debates, only a Teacher preparing his friends for his departure. Judas leaves early, and in the darkness Jesus says words of great love.
observation: “Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end” (13:1).
“If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet” (13:14).
“A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another” (13:34).
“By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another” (13:35).
“Let not your hearts be troubled. Believe in God; believe also in me” (14:1).
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me” (14:6).
“And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper, to be with you forever” (14:16).
“Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you” (14:27).
interpretation:
“Having loved his own… he loved them to the end.” Jesus rises from supper, takes off his outer garments, and wraps a towel around his waist. He pours water into a basin and begins to wash the disciples’ feet, a task for the lowest servant. Peter objects: “You shall never wash my feet.” Jesus replies, “If I do not wash you, you have no share with me.” The washing points to the cleansing that Jesus will accomplish on the cross. Then he explains the example: “If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.” The King serves.

He predicts that one of them will betray him. Judas leaves, and John says, “And it was night.” Jesus then says, “Now is the Son of Man glorified.” He gives the new commandment: love one another as I have loved you. Love is the badge of discipleship. Peter declares that he will lay down his life for Jesus, and Jesus answers that he will deny him three times.

Chapter 14 opens with comfort. “Let not your hearts be troubled.” He is going to prepare a place in his Father’s house, which has many rooms, and he will come again and take them to himself. Thomas objects, “We do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” Jesus replies with the sixth “I AM”: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.” This is the exclusive claim of the gospel and also a great invitation. The way is a person, and he is available to anyone who comes.

Philip asks, “Show us the Father.” Jesus says, “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.” Then comes the promise of the Spirit. Jesus will ask the Father, and he will give another Helper, the Spirit of truth, who dwells with them and will be in them. “I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.” The Spirit will teach them and remind them of all that Jesus said. Finally: “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you.” He leaves them not with an escape from trouble but with his peace.
connection: Exodus 12 is the Passover context of the meal. Isaiah 52:13 and 53:11-12 describe the suffering servant. Psalm 41:9 predicts the betrayal. Leviticus 19:18 is the old love commandment. Isaiah 43:1-2 promises the presence of God in trouble. Ezekiel 36:27 promised the Spirit within. Acts 2 records the coming of the Spirit. Philippians 2:5-8 shows the same servant attitude. 1 John 3:16 and 4:7-12 build on the new commandment.
application:
Find a way to serve someone this week in a hidden, humble way, like washing feet.

Say verse 1 to yourself when you are anxious, and name what troubles your heart.

Thank the Father for Jesus, the way, the truth, and the life. Pray for someone who does not yet know him.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for loving you to the end and washing feet.
Ask him to teach you to serve.
Ask him to help you love others as he has loved you.
